m:centrov: The streets are free to walk. Stavropoleos Monastery is normally open from 9am to 6pm and closes during services (hours from guides, to be confirmed): free entry, cover up. The Hanul lui Manuc courtyard is free to walk through. In the evening and at weekends the Old Town is very crowded and noisy, with music until late.
m:parlament: Open every day from 9am to 5pm (Chamber of Deputies website). Standard tour 85 lei (about €15.90); students aged 19–26 55 lei, children aged 7–18 40 lei. Tickets are only sold on the day, at the ticket office in the «Constantin Brâncuși» exhibition hall (Izvor street 2-4), in cash or by card: they're not sold online. For 1–9 people you must book by phoning +40 733 558 102 or 103 at least a day ahead, Monday to Friday from 9am to 4pm (to visit on a Monday, book the Friday before). Arrive 15 minutes early with your physical ID card or passport: a driving licence is not accepted. The number of rooms you can visit varies depending on events.
m:ateneu: The outside and the square are free to see. The inside can be visited on guided tours on varying dates and times, or with a ticket for a George Enescu Philharmonic concert (programme on fge.org.ro): I couldn't find fixed visiting hours, check before you go.
m:carusel: Open Monday to Wednesday from 10am to 10pm and Thursday to Sunday from 10am to midnight (In Your Pocket; to be confirmed on the website). Entry is free.
m:tarani: Normally open Tuesday to Sunday, usually from 10am to 6pm, and closed on Mondays (hours and prices not checked on the official website, to be confirmed). The ticket cost 12 lei until 2023 (guide): it's probably higher now. Take metro M2 to Piața Victoriei and then walk 5 minutes.
m:arcul: Since 2025 access is permanent: open Tuesday to Sunday from 10am to 6pm, entry 15 lei (about €2.80), reduced 8 lei (March 2025 information from a press article, to be confirmed). Taking photos with your phone is free.
m:satului: From 13 October (2025 winter schedule, to be confirmed for 2026) open every day from 9am to 5pm, last ticket 30 minutes before closing; in summer Wednesday to Sunday from 9am to 7pm. In January 2026 the houses were closed for works and the 50% discounted ticket cost 20 lei, so the full price should be about 40 lei (about €7.50): to be confirmed. Closed at Easter, on 25 and 26 December and on 1 and 2 January. Metro M2 stop: Aviatorilor.
m:herastrau: The park is open all day and entry is free. Nearest stops: metro M2 Aviatorilor or Aurel Vlaicu.
m:cismigiu: Open all day, free entry. In winter the lake may be frozen or empty.
m:cotroceni: After 1 November the museum only opens on Saturday and Sunday, from 9am to 5pm, last entry at 4pm (2025 schedule, to be confirmed for 2026): 70 lei full price (about €13.10), students 17.50 lei, pensioners 35 lei. Tickets at the door on Șoseaua Cotroceni or online (IaBilet, BookTes). In spring and summer visits are also possible on weekdays and the gardens are free. Bring your ID card.
vd:carubere: Bucharest's historic restaurant, in an 1879 neo-Gothic building with painted ceilings, stained glass and wooden staircases: traditional Romanian cooking (sarmale, ciorbă, mici) and house beer. It's famous and often full, but it's one of the very few historic dining rooms still alive.
vp:carubere: Hours from the official website. A typical dish usually costs 40–80 lei (about €8–15) according to guides, menu not seen: to be confirmed. At lunch and dinner there's often a queue, better to book.
vd:lacrimi: An Old Town restaurant serving meat dishes and updated Romanian cooking, in a room with wooden tables. A mid-priced place, more careful than the tourist spots.
vp:lacrimi: Mid-range: a main course is usually around 45–75 lei (about €8.50–14) according to a guide, menu not seen. Hours not checked, to be confirmed.
vd:manuc: The 1808 inn with a two-storey galleried inner courtyard, now a restaurant and café: Romanian cooking (sarmale, tripe ciorbă, tochitură) and live music in the evening. You can walk through the courtyard without eating.
vp:manuc: Dishes around 40–80 lei (about €8–15), menu not seen. Typical hours from a guide (9am–11pm, the kitchen stays open later at weekends): to be confirmed.
vd:crama: An Old Town restaurant with a courtyard and live music every evening, offering traditional Romanian dishes and local wines. A good place to try the country's cooking in a relaxed atmosphere.
vp:crama: Mid-range: 35–65 lei per dish (about €7–12), according to a guide, menu not seen. Hours not checked, to be confirmed.
vd:origo: A specialty coffee bar in the Old Town, known for its filter coffee and banana bread. At weekends there's often a queue in the morning.
vp:origo: A coffee with a cake costs about 15–25 lei (about €3–5), prices from a guide. Hours not checked, to be confirmed.
vd:carusel: The bistro on the top floor of the Carusel bookshop, with simple dishes (including vegetarian) and coffee among the shelves and white galleries. A comfortable, pleasant break right in the Old Town.
vp:carusel: Bookshop hours (the bistro may not follow the same hours): to be confirmed. A light meal is around 40–60 lei (€8–11), price from a guide.
vd:linea: A place with a panoramic terrace on the top floor of a building on Strada Lipscani, good for a break with a drink and a view over the Old Town rooftops.
vp:linea: Rooftop bar hours from a guide (tablejourney.com): to be confirmed. Mid-to-high prices for a coffee or an aperitif; the restaurant has a pricier menu ($$$ range).
vd:doina: A Romanian restaurant in a villa with a garden on Kiseleff avenue, near Piața Victoriei and the Peasant Museum: a handy place for lunch after the museum.
vp:doina: Mid-to-high range for Bucharest: a full meal can exceed 100 lei (about €19), price from a guide, not checked. Hours not checked, to be confirmed.
cd:artamuseo: Romanian and European art in the former Royal Palace, on Calea Victoriei.
cd:storia: The Romanian Treasury and the copy of Trajan's Column.
cd:primaverii: The dictator's private residence, with gold bathrooms and a cinema room.
cx:primaverii: Visits are guided and must be booked.
cd:antipa: The natural history museum with dioramas and a mammoth skeleton.
cd:curtea: The ruins of the princely court where Vlad the Impaler reigned.
cd:mogosoaia: A Brâncovenesc palace on a lake, in a park 14 km from the centre.
cx:mogosoaia: It's outside the city: allow about an extra hour for the round trip.
cd:therme: A large complex of tropical pools north of the city.
cx:therme: It's in Balotești, about 15 km from the centre.
